summary: Refuse host cutover when product roots or nested legacy paths are mount points

schema.detail: No schema, journal, receipt or stored-data format changes.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule or digest changes.

compatibility.detail: Linux host migration preflight enumerates mountinfo and macOS enumerates getfsstat records. Both refuse mounts at or below source and destination roots before mutation, using the same classifier; macOS normalizes canonical and verified Data-volume firmlink spellings. Device-identity and same-filesystem rename backstops remain.

downtime.detail: Mount refusal occurs before service stops or journal writes; no migration is attempted.

manual.detail: Move mounts out of legacy roots before cutover while preserving their data in ordinary legacy directories; restart the legacy daemon for quiescence checks. After cutover, stop Fractal and remount at the corresponding Fractal path without hiding migrated data. Destinations must be absent or empty ordinary directories. Remounting populated data directly at the destination with the legacy root absent or a bridge symlink cannot complete the mover. See docs/st3/macos-installation.md.

recovery.detail: The mover never copies or mounts filesystems. Existing interrupted-journal rollback and committed-migration recovery behavior are unchanged.
